name: MDMA
summary: The clearest case in this library of kinetics that are not proportional. MDMA inhibits the very enzyme that clears it, so the body gets worse at removing it as the dose goes up. Twice the dose is considerably more than twice the exposure, and the second dose of a night is cleared more slowly than the first.
mechanism: Reverses the serotonin transporter, so instead of recycling serotonin the transporter pumps it out — a release rather than a reuptake block. It empties the vesicles rather than modulating their release, which is why the effect has a ceiling, why the depletion afterwards is real, and why redosing produces diminishing euphoria with undiminished physical load.

nonlinear.note: MDMA inhibits CYP2D6, the enzyme that metabolises it, within the first hour — so it suppresses its own clearance. Reported plasma levels rise disproportionately with dose: increasing the dose by half can nearly double the exposure. This model is linear and therefore UNDERSTATES levels at higher doses and after redosing. Treat the curve as a floor, not a prediction.

oral.note: Swallowed, with a notable lag while the stomach empties. The two-hour climb is why people conclude it has not worked and take more — a redose taken at 90 minutes lands on top of a dose that has not finished arriving.

insufflated.note: Faster, but the total exposure is much the same; it is the same amount arriving over a shorter window, which raises the peak without extending the effect.

pathways.name: HMMA
pathways.note: The main route, via CYP2D6 then COMT. This is the pathway MDMA shuts down, which is why clearance falls as the dose rises.

pathways.name: MDA
pathways.note: Active, longer-lived than the parent, and more of a stimulant and less of an empathogen. It contributes to the long, edgy tail of the following morning.

pathways.name: Unchanged renal
pathways.note: A substantial fraction leaves untouched, which is why kidney function and hydration matter here more than for most drugs.

effect_levels.label: Levels where hyperthermia and cardiovascular strain rise sharply

risk: Because clearance falls as the dose rises, exposure from redosing is worse than arithmetic suggests. A second dose does not add a second curve — it adds a second curve that is cleared more slowly, on top of one still being absorbed.

The real acute danger is temperature, not the drug level directly. Hyperthermia is driven by serotonergic thermoregulation plus exertion plus a hot room, and it is what turns a survivable dose into a fatal one.
Hyponatraemia from drinking too much plain water is the other classic harm, and its early symptoms — confusion, nausea, headache — look like the drug.
Serotonergic antidepressants interact in both directions: SSRIs blunt the effect by blocking the transporter, while MAOIs can cause life-threatening serotonin syndrome. See interactions.
